intro.title: Discover Trg Kralja Tomislava
intro.nearby: When visiting Trg Kralja Tomislava, you can easily explore the surrounding landmarks of Zagreb's Green Horseshoe, including Zrinjevac Park and Ban Jelačić Square (Trg bana Jelačića), as well as the Croatian National Theatre and the Botanical Garden.
intro.description: Trg Kralja Tomislava (King Tomislav Square), also known simply as Tomislavac or Tomislavov trg, is one of the most beautiful and prominent urban parks in Zagreb, Croatia. Located right across from the Main Railway Station (Glavni kolodvor), it welcomes visitors with the elegant yellow Art Pavilion and a majestic equestrian monument to King Tomislav, the first King of Croatia. It is the southern gateway of Lenuci's Green Horseshoe, a popular meeting place and a masterpiece of 19th-century landscape architecture.

sections.title: History & Heritage
sections.content: The square is named after Tomislav, crowned the first King of Croatia in 925. Its urban design dates to the late 19th and early 20th centuries, when the city was expanding southwards towards the new railway station. The iconic equestrian statue of King Tomislav, created by sculptor Robert Frangeš-Mihanović, was completed in 1938 and finally unveiled in October 1947, honouring the millennium of the Croatian Kingdom.

sections.title: The King Tomislav Monument
sections.content: The bronze equestrian statue faces the railway station, so every arriving traveller meets the king first. Tomislav (d. c. 928) united the Croatian duchies, repelled the Magyar invasions and was crowned the first king of the Croatian Kingdom in 925. The statue was modelled by Frangeš-Mihanović in 1938, but its unveiling was delayed by disputes and the Second World War until 1947.

sections.title: Location & Landscape
sections.content: Situated in the Lower Town of Zagreb, the square forms the southern end of Lenuci's Green Horseshoe – a U-shaped chain of squares and parks designed by city planner Milan Lenuci. The square features meticulously maintained lawns, colourful flower beds and shaded pathways, with the historicist Glavni kolodvor railway station (1892) closing the vista to the south.

sections.title: Architecture & Surroundings
sections.content: The northern end of the square is dominated by the Art Pavilion (Umjetnički paviljon), an elegant yellow exhibition hall originally built for the 1896 Budapest Millennium Exhibition and re-erected in Zagreb in 1898. Around the square stand classicist and secessionist buildings that define Zagreb's Lower Town, including the Croatian State Archives and the Hotel Esplanade (1925).

sections.title: Urban Significance
sections.content: As part of the protected historical urban ensemble of Zagreb, Trg Kralja Tomislava plays a central role in the city's social and cultural life. It frequently hosts open-air concerts, exhibitions and cultural events, and it is the classic first sight of Zagreb for travellers arriving by train.

sections.title: Events & Advent
sections.content: During Advent in Zagreb – repeatedly voted one of Europe's best Christmas markets – the square has hosted the Zagreb Ice Park, a large outdoor skating rink surrounded by lights and stalls. In summer it turns into a green oasis for concerts, picnics and relaxation.

history.title: History in a Timeline
history.subtitle: From a Croatian king to a beloved city park

timeline.title: A kingdom is born
timeline.text: Tomislav is crowned the first King of Croatia with papal blessing. Around 928 he dies, and the cause of his death remains a mystery to this day.

timeline.title: The railway arrives
timeline.text: The first train enters Zagreb (then about 40,000 inhabitants), connecting the city with Vienna and Budapest and shaping the future railway quarter.

timeline.title: Glavni kolodvor opens
timeline.text: The historicist Main Railway Station, designed by Hungarian railway engineer Ferenc Pfaff, is completed and closes the southern side of the future square.

timeline.title: The Art Pavilion arrives
timeline.text: Built for the Budapest Millennium Exhibition, the metal-frame Art Pavilion is dismantled, shipped by train to Zagreb and re-opened in 1898 as Croatia's first purpose-built exhibition hall.

timeline.title: Monument to King Tomislav
timeline.text: Sculptor Robert Frangeš-Mihanović completes the equestrian statue in 1938. After years of disputes and the Second World War, the monument is finally unveiled in October 1947.

timeline.title: Zagreb's green living room
timeline.text: The square hosts concerts, markets and the Advent ice park. For generations of travellers, the view of the statue, the Art Pavilion, the cathedral towers and Medvednica hill is the first postcard of Zagreb.

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.subtitle: A park that welcomes everyone
accessibility.note: Trg Kralja Tomislava is an open public space with level, paved paths throughout.

items.text: Flat paved pathways across the whole park; the monument and Art Pavilion are reached at ground level.
Smooth, wide paths suit strollers; the route from the station tram stop is step-free.
Tram stops and the station entrance sit right beside the square, with level boarding on most routes.
Benches, shaded lawns and accessible public toilets are available at the neighbouring station.

etiquette.title: Visitor Etiquette
etiquette.subtitle: How to enjoy the park respectfully
etiquette.note: These are general guidelines for a protected urban green space.
dos: Walk on the paved paths and sit only on the lawns marked for relaxing
Photograph freely – the monument and the Art Pavilion are the classic postcard views
Keep dogs on a lead and clean up after them
Use the bins provided and take your litter with you
donts: Do not climb on the monument or its pedestal
Do not pick flowers or walk on the flower beds
Do not ride bicycles or scooters through the lawns
Do not disturb concerts, events or other visitors

items.name: The classic postcard
items.tip: Stand at the station side of the square at golden hour so the king, the Art Pavilion and the cathedral towers line up.

items.name: Across the lawns
items.tip: Low-angle shots over the flower beds frame the monument against the sky.

items.name: Art Pavilion front
items.tip: The yellow facade photographs best in soft morning or late-afternoon light, before the square falls into shadow.

items.name: Seasonal views
items.tip: During Advent the ice rink and lights create unique night shots; in autumn the tree colours line the pathways.

items.title: A thousand years for one statue
items.text: The equestrian statue of King Tomislav was completed in 1938, but the unveiling was postponed again and again – first by long disputes over its design and placement, then by the Second World War. The monument finally reached its pedestal in October 1947.

items.title: The pavilion that came by train
items.text: The Art Pavilion was originally built for the 1896 Budapest Millennium Exhibition. After the fair it was dismantled, loaded onto trains and re-erected on Trg Kralja Tomislava, opening in 1898 with a grand exhibition of contemporary artists.

items.title: The first sight of Zagreb
items.text: For generations, the first thing travellers see when leaving Glavni kolodvor is the king on horseback, the yellow Art Pavilion, the cathedral towers and the green slopes of Medvednica – the classic arrival postcard of Zagreb.

items.title: Tomislavac – the people's name
items.text: Locals rarely say the full name: the square is simply 'Tomislavac' or 'Tomislavov trg'. It is the southern gate of Lenuci's Green Horseshoe, where the Lower Town's chain of parks begins – or ends.

items.title: Winter magic: the Ice Park
items.text: During Advent in Zagreb, the square often turns into a large open-air skating rink. Ice skaters glide beneath the king's statue while the Art Pavilion glows behind the festive lights – a picture that has made Zagreb famous across Europe.

items.title: The mystery of the king's death
items.text: King Tomislav, who united Croatia, died around 928 – barely three years after his coronation. Chronicles do not explain how or why he died, and to this day the mystery fuels legends about the man the square is named after.

nearby.title: Nearby Attractions
nearby.subtitle: What to combine with your visit

items.name: Zrinjevac Park
items.text: The next green link of the Green Horseshoe, famous for its plane trees, fountains and the 19th-century meteorological column.

items.name: Ban Jelačić Square (Trg bana Jelačića)
items.text: Zagreb's main square and meeting point, with the statue of Ban Josip Jelačić and the start of the pedestrian shopping street Ilica.

items.name: Croatian National Theatre (HNK)
items.text: A magnificent neo-baroque theatre building further along the Green Horseshoe, with guided tours and a rich performance programme.

items.name: Zagreb Main Station (Glavni kolodvor)
items.text: The 1892 historicist station building is right opposite the square – convenient arrival and departure point for your visit.

items.name: Botanical Garden
items.text: A green oasis in the Lower Town with thousands of plant species, ponds and a small glasshouse (seasonal opening).

items.name: Museum of Arts and Crafts
items.text: One of Zagreb's most beautiful secessionist buildings, displaying applied arts and design collections in a historicist interior.

items.question: What are the opening hours of Trg Kralja Tomislava?
items.answer: As a public city park, Trg Kralja Tomislava is open 24/7, free of charge. However, the nearby Art Pavilion and other attractions have their own specific visiting hours.

items.question: Is there an entrance fee?
items.answer: No. The park, the monument and the lawns are completely free and open to the public at all times.

items.question: Are there guided tours available?
items.answer: The park itself doesn't offer official tours, but many Zagreb city walking tours – especially those covering the Green Horseshoe – include Trg Kralja Tomislava in their itineraries.

items.question: Is the site accessible for wheelchair users?
items.answer: Yes. The square features flat, paved pathways that are fully accessible for wheelchair users and strollers. The nearest tram stops are right at the station.

items.question: How do I get from the Main Railway Station to the square?
items.answer: Simply walk out of the station's main entrance – the square is directly opposite, just across the street. Tram lines 2, 4, 6, 9 and 13 stop at 'Glavni kolodvor'.

items.question: Is the Advent ice rink really on this square?
items.answer: During Advent in Zagreb, the square has hosted the Zagreb Ice Park – a large open-air skating rink. Availability and dates change every season, so check the official Advent in Zagreb programme.

items.question: Can I visit the Art Pavilion on the square?
items.answer: Yes. The Art Pavilion (Umjetnički paviljon) is an active exhibition hall at Trg Kralja Tomislava 22, with a changing programme of contemporary and classical exhibitions. Check its official website for current opening hours and tickets.

items.question: Are dogs allowed in the park?
items.answer: Yes. As a public park, Trg Kralja Tomislava generally welcomes dogs on a lead. Please keep your dog on a leash and clean up after it, as in any Zagreb park.

items.question: Can I sit on the grass or have a picnic?
items.answer: The lawns are open for sitting and relaxing during the day. Please keep off the flower beds, use the bins provided and leave the grass as you found it.

items.question: Is the square safe at night?
items.answer: Trg Kralja Tomislava is a well-lit public space in the city centre and is generally considered safe at night. As anywhere in a large city, stay aware of your surroundings and keep to well-used routes.

transport.title: How to Get Here
transport.fromCenterDesc: A short 10–15 minute walk south through the parks of the Green Horseshoe, or two tram stops on lines 6 or 13.
transport.fromStationDesc: Located immediately opposite the main entrance – just cross the street and you are on the square.
transport.fromAirportDesc: Take the airport shuttle bus to the main bus station (Autobusni kolodvor), then tram lines 2 or 6 a few stops to Glavni kolodvor.
transport.publicTransportDesc: Tram lines 2, 4, 6, 9 and 13 stop directly at 'Glavni kolodvor' (Main Station), right next to the square.
transport.walkingDesc: Easily walkable from all central Zagreb locations; the square lies on the main pedestrian axis of the Lower Town.
transport.drivingDesc: Follow signs to Glavni kolodvor. Street parking is limited; use the nearby public garages.

route.title: Recommended Route
route.overview: A classic walk along the eastern arm of the Green Horseshoe, from the station to the heart of the Lower Town.
steps: Arrive at Glavni kolodvor (Main Railway Station) and cross the street
Admire the King Tomislav equestrian monument facing the station
Stroll through the central lawns and flower beds of the park
Take photos in front of the yellow Art Pavilion
Continue north along the Green Horseshoe to Zrinjevac Park
Finish at Ban Jelačić Square and the historic Upper Town
